**CONFIDENTIAL — INTERNAL MEMORANDUM**

**TO:** Ownership, Indy Roof & Restoration
**FROM:** Chief Marketing Officer
**DATE:** May 14, 2025
**RE:** 90-Day Offensive Strategy — Taking Market Share from Raptor Roofing

---

**SITUATION BRIEF**

We hold 2,195 reviews at 4.9 stars. Raptor holds 671 at 5.0. On paper, they have a star-rating edge. In volume — the metric that drives LSA rank, consumer trust, and market perception — we dominate them by more than 3-to-1. 

LSA ranking is heavily weighted by star rating and the number of reviews.

 That asymmetry is our most powerful weapon and we are not using it aggressively enough. Here is how we change that this quarter.

---

**SECTION 1: WHERE RAPTOR IS VULNERABLE**

**Weakness 1: Single-Channel Lead Dependency**

Raptor's primary lead sources are Google LSA and Google Ads — full stop. 

The contractors getting crushed right now all have the same profile: they built their entire lead generation around one paid channel. When that channel gets more expensive and less effective, they have nowhere to go except spend more.

 

Roofing LSA costs now run $55–$90 per lead, with storm damage queries hitting $150 or more in active weather zones.

 **Raptor is renting leads from Google. We need to make that rent feel unbearable by owning the organic and earned channels they are ignoring.**

**Weakness 2: Thin Geographic Roots Outside Center Grove and Greenwood**

Raptor has deliberately concentrated its community identity in Greenwood and Center Grove. That is smart micro-positioning — but it is also a ceiling. It leaves Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Avon, Brownsburg, and Mooresville comparatively uncontested from their brand. Their own website lists these markets but offers no localized content, no neighborhood-specific proof, no community ties. **Their brand identity is geographically narrow. We can establish dominant local presence in six surrounding submarkets before they react.**

**Weakness 3: A 5.0 Rating Is a Trap — And Their Volume Gap Is Catastrophic**

671 reviews is a thin foundation for a "premium" brand claim in a metro of two million people. A 5.0 with 671 reviews statistically signals a brand that is either early-stage or one that aggressively manages negative reviews out of public view. 

91% of homeowners rely on online reviews before choosing a contractor.

 When a homeowner compares Raptor's 671 reviews to our 2,195, the psychological authority gap is irreversible at the point of decision. **We must make that comparison unavoidable in our ad creative and landing pages.** Additionally, Raptor's brand "accountability" messaging has no third-party verification layer — no GuildQuality profile with external data, no volume of cross-platform reviews. Our depth of proof across platforms is superior; we are simply not weaponizing it.

---

**SECTION 2: THREE 90-DAY CAMPAIGNS**

**Campaign 1: "2,000+ Reasons" — Volume Dominance Ad Blitz**

Launch a Google Ads and Meta campaign directly targeting Greenwood, Center Grove, Carmel, and Fishers zip codes with a single creative hook: **"2,000+ families in Central Indiana trusted us with their roof. See why."** The ad links to neighborhood-specific landing pages showing real job photos, real homeowner names, and review counts by zip code. This is not a comparison ad — it does not name Raptor. It simply makes our social proof so visible and localized that Raptor's numbers look thin by comparison. Run Performance Max alongside standard search to capture the full funnel. 

Maximize the Google Business Profile with weekly updates, real job photos, accurate service listings, and every review responded to within 24 hours. Businesses with active GBPs saw 28% more discovery search views within 90 days.



**Campaign 2: Nextdoor + Neighborhood Facebook Group Infiltration in Center Grove and Greenwood**

This is their home turf. We take it. Assign two dedicated field marketers to saturate Center Grove and Greenwood neighborhood Facebook groups and Nextdoor with genuine project posts — before/after photos, real customer names, hyperlocal testimonials. Simultaneously, run Nextdoor Neighborhood Ads in these exact zip codes. 

By targeting specific neighborhoods, especially those where you are already working, you create geographic relevance and social proof. Unlike shared leads from third-party providers, you are not competing with multiple other roofers for the same prospect.

 Every crew truck in those neighborhoods gets a door hanger dropped on adjacent homes. Cost per lead for this channel is a fraction of LSA. **We do not need to outspend Raptor in their backyard. We need to out-show them.**

**Campaign 3: AI Search and GBP Domination Play**

Raptor's website content is thin on educational depth. Ours needs to be the resource Google AI and ChatGPT cite when homeowners ask about Indianapolis roofing. Immediately commission 12 location-specific blog articles targeting: "best roofers in Carmel IN," "hail damage roof claim Greenwood IN," "how long does a roof replacement take in Indianapolis," and equivalent queries for every submarket Raptor claims but doesn't own. 

When ChatGPT or Google AI Mode recommends a contractor, it pulls from websites that answer real questions. "How much does a furnace replacement cost in Charlotte?" beats "We provide quality HVAC service" every single time.

 Pair this with a dedicated Google Business Profile posting schedule — one post every three days, every post geotagged, every post with a real job photo.

---

**SECTION 3: THE SINGLE MOST THREATENING MOVE THIS QUARTER**

**Launch a hyper-targeted LSA and Google Ads campaign bidding directly on Raptor's branded adjacent keywords — "Raptor Roofing reviews," "Raptor Roofing Indianapolis," "Raptor Roofing vs" — and route that traffic to a landing page titled: "Comparing Indianapolis Roofers? Here's What 2,195 Reviews Look Like."**

The page shows no competitor names. It shows our review volume, our cross-platform presence, our years in market since 2018, our BBB A+ standing, and a side-by-side of what 671 reviews versus 2,195 reviews actually means in terms of completed jobs and homeowner confidence. 

There is a fixed number of LSA leads in every roofing market, influenced by demand, seasonality, and competition.

 Every lead we intercept from a homeowner researching Raptor is a lead that costs Raptor money — they paid to generate that consumer's awareness, and we convert it.

**Cameron should be uncomfortable not because we are attacking his brand. He should be uncomfortable because we are making his review gap the centerpiece of every homeowner's decision — and he cannot fix 671 versus 2,195 in 90 days.**

This is where we win.

---

*Prepared for internal strategic use only. Recommend immediate budget alignment meeting within 5 business days.*

**Launch a "Insurance Coverage Audit" lead magnet this week targeting the 2005-2015 housing stock in Greenwood and Center Grove, before SPG turns its Roofing Contractor #92 ranking into paid creative.**

SPG just got a national third-party credential they can wave around (#92 on the 2025 Top 100, up from #128). Trying to out-credential them is a losing game we don't need to play this quarter. The asymmetric counter is to own the single highest-intent conversation no one in this market is having at scale: the RCV-to-ACV cliff and the RPS endorsements insurers are quietly slipping into renewals on roofs as young as 10 years. Greenwood and Center Grove housing stock is sitting right in the 10-20 year sweet spot, which means tens of thousands of homeowners in our service area are about to discover their policy pays half of what they think it does — and the contractor who tells them first wins the relationship before there's even a storm.

Execution this week: build a one-page offer ("Free 15-Minute Insurance Coverage Check — we read your declarations page and inspect your roof, no obligation"), wire it to a dedicated landing page with a Calendly slot, and push it through three channels by Friday: (1) a $1,500 geofenced Meta campaign targeting homeowners 35+ in the 46142/46143/46143 ZIPs, (2) a door-hanger drop on 500 homes in two target subdivisions with the RPS one-pager attached, and (3) an email to the past-customer list asking them to forward to neighbors. The script for reps is the moat — one hour of training, one laminated cheat sheet covering RCV vs ACV vs RPS, percentage-based deductibles. Most competitors are not having this conversation; SPG, Bone Dry, and Amos are still selling shingles.

Success metric this week: 25 booked coverage-check appointments and 8 inspections completed. Track close rate separately — these should run hotter than cold leads because we're showing up as an advocate, not a vendor.

---

**Deploy review-request automation across SMS and email tied to job completion, with a goal of closing the velocity gap on Indy Roof & Restoration (+76/30d) and Amos (+99/30d) within 90 days.**

Here's the uncomfortable number: at +17 reviews in the last 30 days, we are being out-paced 4-to-1 by Amos and 4.5-to-1 by Indy Roof in raw review velocity. Our 5.0 average is the prettiest in the top 10, but Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode are now surfacing one to three businesses by name, and the Roofing Webmasters data shows multi-platform review presence is the single strongest correlator with AI citation. We are leaving citations on the table every week we don't compound. Worse, Indy Roof just published a self-serving "Top 10 Roofing Companies in Indianapolis for 2026" listicle ranking themselves #1 on the strength of their review volume — that's the exact ammo AI systems will scrape and cite.

Execution this week: stand up a review request automation in whatever CRM/comms stack we're already running (NiceJob, Podium, BirdEye, or even just a Zapier-to-Twilio build if budget is tight — under $400/month either way). Trigger: job marked complete in the field. Sequence: SMS at 2 hours post-completion with a direct Google review link, email at 24 hours with the same link plus Facebook and Yelp options, second SMS at 72 hours only if no review posted. Audit Yelp and Facebook profiles in parallel — if either has under 50 reviews, route 30% of the asks there instead of Google to thicken the multi-platform footprint AI is rewarding.

Success metric: hit +30 Google reviews in the next 30 days (nearly doubling current velocity) and add a minimum of 15 reviews split across Yelp and Facebook in the same window. The compounding math gets us past Trojan and Richmond on volume by end of Q2 while widening the quality gap.

---

**Sign a hyperlocal community-anchor partnership this week that Bone Dry's 17-location footprint can never authentically match.**

Bone Dry is a real long-term threat — 30 years of brand recall in this market, 2,400+ reviews on the main location, Owens Corning Platinum and CertainTeed ShingleMaster both. We don't out-spend them on awareness. We out-local them. Bone Dry is headquartered in Indy but operates Colorado to Florida; they cannot credibly be "Greenwood's roofer" no matter how much they spend, and that's the gap to exploit while we're still small enough to be specific.

Execution this week: lock in one anchor partnership in Greenwood or Center Grove that puts the Raptor name in front of homeowners in a non-advertising context. Three candidates to pursue by Friday: (1) title sponsor for Greenwood Freedom Festival or the next Center Grove HS athletic season — even a $5K-$10K commitment gets logo placement and PA reads to thousands of exactly our demo, (2) a co-branded "free roof check before winter" event with a respected local insurance broker who is also seeing the ACV/RPS issue blow up at claim time and wants an honest contractor to refer to, or (3) a standing relationship with two or three top-producing Johnson County realtors to be their default pre-listing roof inspection contractor (free 10-minute inspections in exchange for being the recommended roofer at closing). Option 2 is the highest-leverage because it directly compounds the insurance-audit play in Action 1.

Success metric this week: one signed partnership agreement (verbal commitment + follow-up email is fine) and a calendar date for the first joint touchpoint within 30 days. Measure downstream by tagged lead source over the following 90 days — target 15 partnership-sourced leads in Q2.

# Competitive Intelligence Brief: Amos Exteriors
**Raptor Roofing | Cameron Blakely Dashboard | Refreshed: May 19, 2025**

---

## 1. Who They Are



Founded in 1971, Amos Exteriors is a leading exterior remodeling company trusted by homeowners and businesses throughout Central Indiana.

 

Family-owned and operated, they hold GAF Master Elite Contractor status, maintain an A+ BBB rating, and are members of the NRCA and Indianapolis Apartment Association.

 They are not a roofing-only shop — 

they offer GAF asphalt shingles, slate, cedar shake, and flat roofing systems, and carry GAF's System Plus Warranty

 — while also competing across siding, windows, doors, gutters, and commercial coatings. Their scale, age, and multi-trade footprint make them the most institutionally entrenched competitor in the Indy market.

---

## 2. Estimated Scale



RocketReach puts Amos at $28.6M annual revenue (2025 estimate) with 57 employees.

 That is the highest third-party revenue figure found; Prospeo and LeadIQ show lower estimates in the $10-12M range, likely undercounting subcontractor-heavy revenue. **Confidence: medium.** 

Their sales department alone is listed at 21 employees, led by a Director of Sales (Matt O.),

 which implies a serious, structured sales org. 

A 2020 PPP loan of $584,200 from Stock Yards Bank cited retention of 40 jobs,

 which anchors the headcount floor. The $20-30M revenue band is the most defensible working estimate given the multi-trade footprint and 54-year operating history.

---

## 3. Recent Hiring Signals



ZipRecruiter shows an open "Team Lead, Field Marketing" role in Indianapolis.

 

Their own careers page is actively recruiting Home Improvement Sales Consultants, with reps running both company-provided leads and self-generated referrals.

 

ZoomInfo flags an open Estimator & Project Manager role in Indianapolis.

 The field marketing team lead posting is the most telling signal — they are investing in door-to-door and neighborhood canvassing infrastructure at the leadership level, not just rep headcount. 

Indeed reviews from reps flag that leads can involve 1.5-hour drives for low-value appointments, and that canvassers set for almost anything,

 suggesting lead quality control is a current operational weakness underneath the growth push.

---

## 4. Off-Google Presence



Amos holds only 2.5 stars on Yelp

, against their 4.9 on Google and 3,093 Google reviews. That is a textbook review-funneling gap — they are clearly steering satisfied customers to Google and leaving Yelp to organic, unmanaged outcomes. 

They have been BBB Accredited since September 19, 1993, and carry an A+ rating.

 

BBB lists Robert Amos as Owner, Bruce McClain as Director of Marketing, and Jana Perrott as Marketing Manager

 — a notably staffed marketing function for a regional contractor. Their Facebook presence exists at [facebook.com/AmosExteriors](https://www.facebook.com/AmosExteriors). No active Facebook Ad Library campaigns were surfaced in search results, but with a dedicated marketing director and manager on staff, paid social is likely running. Nextdoor presence was not surfaced and should be monitored directly.

---

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture



Their tech stack includes Yoast SEO, WP Rocket, Open Graph, and Google Maps integration

 — a competent but off-the-shelf WordPress setup, not a custom SEO architecture. They have invested heavily in location-specific landing pages: dedicated URLs for [Indianapolis](https://www.amosexteriors.com/locations/indianapolis-in), [Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Greenwood, and Zionsville](https://www.amosexteriors.com/service-areas/indianapolis), which is the right AEO move for suburb-level queries. 

Their GAF profile also enumerates those exact suburbs — Zionsville, Carmel, Noblesville, Westfield, Fishers, Geist, Plainfield, Avon, Greenwood, and more

 — creating consistent entity signals across authoritative domains. They carry a blog, and their 54-year history with BBB, NRCA, and GAF generates meaningful legacy backlink authority. The site runs on WordPress with standard schema. The Yoast plugin is entry-level schema implementation; there is no evidence of advanced FAQ/HowTo schema that would feed AI Overviews directly.

---

## 6. Generative Engine Visibility

Amos Exteriors is a strong candidate to appear in AI-generated roofing recommendations for Indianapolis due to three compounding factors: 3,093 Google reviews at 4.9 stars, 54 years of indexed web presence, and consistent multi-directory citations (GAF, BBB, Angi, Yelp, NRCA). 

AI tools pull simultaneously from a company's website, Google Business Profile, reviews across platforms, and other online mentions — looking for agreement across those sources

 — and Amos has more of that cross-platform footprint than nearly any Indy roofer. However, their Yelp 2.5-star discrepancy is a negative signal that AI models may surface. Raptor's 673 reviews at a perfect 5.0 and a cleaner cross-platform consistency is a structural AEO advantage if Cameron continues building suburb-specific content with schema markup. 

AI models cite content with factual density, schema markup, and clear section headers

 — Amos's WordPress/Yoast setup covers the basics but likely underperforms on structured answer content. Raptor has a clear lane to own AI citations for premium, accountability-first positioning.

---

## 7. Strategic Read vs. Raptor

**Where Amos beats Raptor:** Raw review volume (3,093 vs. 673), legacy domain authority from 54 years of citations, a named marketing department (Director + Manager), a 21-person structured sales team, multi-trade bundling that increases average ticket size, and a Lafayette second location extending geographic reach. Their institutional depth is difficult to replicate quickly.

**Where Raptor beats Amos:** Perfect 5.0 star rating is objectively cleaner than Amos's 4.9, and Raptor's 0.95 owner response rate versus Amos's Yelp neglect tells a different accountability story. Raptor's "we don't outsource accountability" positioning is sharper and more defensible than Amos's broad multi-trade messaging.

**Most exploitable weakness:** Amos's Yelp 2.5-star score against their 4.9 Google rating is a credibility crack Cameron can exploit directly in sales conversations and in targeted content — "check us on every platform" is a line Raptor can run that Amos absolutely cannot.

---

## 8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy

1. **Suburb-specific landing pages with GAF/manufacturer cross-linking.** Amos has built out location pages for every major Indy suburb and cross-referenced them with their GAF certified contractor profile. That double-indexed, authoritative citation structure feeds both traditional SEO and AI recommendations. Cameron should audit whether Raptor's suburb pages are being cross-referenced on GAF, Owens Corning, and BBB profiles at the same granularity.

2. **Field Marketing Team Lead structure.** Amos is hiring leadership for canvassing, not just canvassers. That means they are building a repeatable, managed neighborhood-blitz system — likely triggered post-storm. Cameron should watch whether Amos's canvassing activity follows hail/wind events and consider whether a structured storm-response field presence (even a smaller one) belongs in Raptor's lead gen mix.

3. **Multi-trade bundling as average ticket lever.** 

Amos markets roof replacement, gutter installation, siding, windows, attic insulation, and painting as an integrated offering

, which meaningfully raises average job value. Even if Raptor stays roofing-focused, positioning a preferred-partner referral network (trusted window, gutter, siding subs) could defend against customers who want a single accountable contact — and deny Amos the cross-sell at the point of roof sale.

## **1. Who They Are**

 Their differentiator is breadth, not depth: 

services span roofing (flat and sloped), siding, windows, doors, awnings, guttering, fencing, decking, and railing

Richmond Guttering/Exteriors received an SBA PPP loan of $686,499 from Centier Bank, resulting in the retention of 65 jobs

 — which is the most reliable headcount anchor available. **Confidence: medium** (PPP data is circa 2020-21; current headcount may have shifted).

, indicating minimal investment in employer brand and a relatively small professional footprint online. At 65 retained employees and a multi-trade model, estimated annual revenue is likely in the $8M–$14M range. **Confidence: low** — no current ZoomInfo revenue figure is publicly surfaced without a paid pull.

## **3. Recent Hiring Signals**

 — but no active open roles are publicly visible on Indeed or LinkedIn as of this refresh.

, but no new postings in the last 30 days are surfaced. No marketing, sales leadership, or ops leadership hiring signals detected. This is a quiet hiring posture — either they're fully staffed, running lean, or hiring off-market.

---

## **4. Off-Google Presence**

The cross-platform review picture reveals a meaningful gap. Their Google profile carries 610 reviews at 4.5 stars. 

On Yelp, they have only 23 reviews

 — classic review-funneling behavior where happy customers get directed to Google while Yelp collects the organic, often dissatisfied, overflow. 

Facebook shows 47 reviews at a 92% recommendation rate

, which is a softer signal but consistent with an older customer base that uses Facebook. 

BBB rates them A+ and they have been accredited since 1994

 — a genuine longevity asset. However, the BBB complaint file is not clean: 

at least one customer stated they took legal action against Richmond and received a $65,000 settlement for damages caused.

 

Angi rates them 4.2 out of 5

, and 

they do not offer emergency services according to Angi

 — a notable gap for storm-season lead capture. The Yelp-to-Google ratio (23 vs. 610 reviews) is the clearest funneling signal in the market.

---

## **5. SEO and AEO Posture**

Richmond operates under the domain [richmondguttering.com](https://www.richmondguttering.com) — a legacy domain name rooted in gutters, not roofing, which is a structural SEO liability for anyone targeting "roof replacement Indianapolis" queries at the top of the funnel. Their site runs on WordPress (

confirmed via ZoomInfo technology stack detection, which also lists Facebook Pixel and Facebook Web Custom Audiences as active tools

). Their roofing service page ([richmondguttering.com/roofing/](https://www.richmondguttering.com/roofing/)) exists but is thin — it reads as a feature list with minimal long-form content or FAQ schema. No evidence of a structured blog publishing cadence targeting Indy suburb keywords (Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Zionsville). The domain's age (1987-era brand) likely gives it some authority, but the mismatch between domain name and primary service intent is an exploitable SEO gap for Raptor.

## **6. Generative Engine Visibility**

Based on analysis of current AI answer patterns for queries like "best roofers Indianapolis," "roof replacement Carmel Indiana," and "roofing company Fishers Noblesville Zionsville": Richmond Exteriors is not consistently surfaced as a named citation in generative engine responses (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude). Their domain-name mismatch (richmondguttering.com for a roofing query) likely suppresses LLM confidence in categorizing them as a roofing specialist. They have volume — 610 Google reviews — but the 4.5 star average, the BBB complaint history, and the generalist brand identity dilute the trust signals that LLMs weight when constructing recommendation lists. This is a live opportunity: Raptor's tighter roofing-specific positioning and 5.0 rating are exactly the signals that AEO-optimized content can leverage to own named citations in AI answers.

---

## **7. Strategic Read vs. Raptor**

**Where they beat Raptor:** Brand longevity (38 years) and service breadth give them cross-sell leverage — a customer who gets a roof can become a fence and gutter customer, which Raptor doesn't capture. Their BBB accreditation since 1994 carries weight with older homeowner segments.

**Where Raptor beats them:** Raptor holds 673 reviews at a perfect 5.0 versus Richmond's 610 at 4.5 — a meaningful quality gap, not just a rounding difference. Raptor's review velocity (14 in 30 days) is competitive with Richmond's identical 14-in-30 pace, but Raptor's zero-defect rating compounds over time. Richmond's 85% owner response rate is decent but not exceptional, and their BBB complaint log including a $65K legal settlement is permanently indexed, searchable, and citable.

 This is on their homepage and roofing pages. If Raptor has financing available, it should be positioned just as prominently — not buried in the proposal stage. Loss of deals to financing competitors happens before the estimate call.

## 7. Strategic Read vs. Raptor

**Where they beat Raptor:** Raw review volume (2,153 vs. 664) dominates every Google Local Pack ranking signal and almost certainly drives their AI citation frequency. Their editorial policy infrastructure is ahead of anything most residential roofers in the market have built. Their insurance-claim navigation positioning gives them a clear hook for storm-damage leads that Raptor does not explicitly own.

**Where Raptor beats them:** 5.0 star rating vs. 4.9 is a real differentiator at the premium end of the market — particularly with higher-income homeowners in Carmel, Zionsville, and Westfield who read reviews closely. Raptor's "we don't outsource accountability" positioning is harder to attack than a volume-first brand. 

IRR has documented BBB complaints involving alleged requests for review removal tied to dispute resolution and property damage claims

 — that is a specific, citable service execution gap. 

One BBB reviewer reported roofwork already coming up less than a year after installation

 — workmanship liability that Raptor's premium positioning directly counters.

**Most exploitable weakness:** Their Google-to-Yelp review ratio (2,153 vs. 28) signals a review-funnel operation that leaves them exposed on any platform they don't control — and their BBB complaint record contains substantive execution failures that Raptor can indirectly reference through "accountability" messaging without naming them directly.

---

## 8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy

**1. The Editorial Policy play for AEO.** IRR's site includes a published editorial and fact-checking policy — a tactic borrowed from media sites that dramatically improves AI citation eligibility. Cameron should task the web team with adding equivalent structured trust content to [raptorroofing.com](https://raptorroofing.com) within 30 days. This is low-cost and high-leverage for generative engine visibility.

**2. The 1% revenue-to-charity pledge as a public commitment.** 

IRR publicly commits 1% of all revenue to Indiana charities including Habitat for Humanity, Toys for Tots, Isiah117, and Fountains of Hope.

 This is a documented, named pledge — not a vague "we give back" line — and it converts into local press, Nextdoor goodwill, and referral credibility with real estate agents. Raptor should formalize and name any existing charitable activity with the same specificity.

**3. Real estate agent partnership as a structured channel.** 

IRR explicitly cites being "trusted by real estate agents" as a core part of their service positioning.

 

Their org chart includes a named Branch Manager,

 suggesting they have a dedicated relationship-management function. Raptor should audit whether any systematic RE agent referral program exists and, if not, treat this as a near-term revenue channel — particularly in Carmel and Zionsville where transaction volume and roof replacement rates are high.

red_team.memo:
**CONFIDENTIAL — INTERNAL MEMORANDUM**

**TO:** Ownership, Indy Roof & Restoration
**FROM:** Chief Marketing Officer
**DATE:** May 14, 2025
**RE:** 90-Day Offensive Strategy — Taking Market Share from Raptor Roofing

---

**SITUATION BRIEF**

We hold 2,195 reviews at 4.9 stars. Raptor holds 671 at 5.0. On paper, they have a star-rating edge. In volume — the metric that drives LSA rank, consumer trust, and market perception — we dominate them by more than 3-to-1. 

LSA ranking is heavily weighted by star rating and the number of reviews.

 That asymmetry is our most powerful weapon and we are not using it aggressively enough. Here is how we change that this quarter.

---

**SECTION 1: WHERE RAPTOR IS VULNERABLE**

**Weakness 1: Single-Channel Lead Dependency**

Raptor's primary lead sources are Google LSA and Google Ads — full stop. 

The contractors getting crushed right now all have the same profile: they built their entire lead generation around one paid channel. When that channel gets more expensive and less effective, they have nowhere to go except spend more.

 

Roofing LSA costs now run $55–$90 per lead, with storm damage queries hitting $150 or more in active weather zones.

 **Raptor is renting leads from Google. We need to make that rent feel unbearable by owning the organic and earned channels they are ignoring.**

**Weakness 2: Thin Geographic Roots Outside Center Grove and Greenwood**

Raptor has deliberately concentrated its community identity in Greenwood and Center Grove. That is smart micro-positioning — but it is also a ceiling. It leaves Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Avon, Brownsburg, and Mooresville comparatively uncontested from their brand. Their own website lists these markets but offers no localized content, no neighborhood-specific proof, no community ties. **Their brand identity is geographically narrow. We can establish dominant local presence in six surrounding submarkets before they react.**

**Weakness 3: A 5.0 Rating Is a Trap — And Their Volume Gap Is Catastrophic**

671 reviews is a thin foundation for a "premium" brand claim in a metro of two million people. A 5.0 with 671 reviews statistically signals a brand that is either early-stage or one that aggressively manages negative reviews out of public view. 

91% of homeowners rely on online reviews before choosing a contractor.

 When a homeowner compares Raptor's 671 reviews to our 2,195, the psychological authority gap is irreversible at the point of decision. **We must make that comparison unavoidable in our ad creative and landing pages.** Additionally, Raptor's brand "accountability" messaging has no third-party verification layer — no GuildQuality profile with external data, no volume of cross-platform reviews. Our depth of proof across platforms is superior; we are simply not weaponizing it.

---

**SECTION 2: THREE 90-DAY CAMPAIGNS**

**Campaign 1: "2,000+ Reasons" — Volume Dominance Ad Blitz**

Launch a Google Ads and Meta campaign directly targeting Greenwood, Center Grove, Carmel, and Fishers zip codes with a single creative hook: **"2,000+ families in Central Indiana trusted us with their roof. See why."** The ad links to neighborhood-specific landing pages showing real job photos, real homeowner names, and review counts by zip code. This is not a comparison ad — it does not name Raptor. It simply makes our social proof so visible and localized that Raptor's numbers look thin by comparison. Run Performance Max alongside standard search to capture the full funnel. 

Maximize the Google Business Profile with weekly updates, real job photos, accurate service listings, and every review responded to within 24 hours. Businesses with active GBPs saw 28% more discovery search views within 90 days.



**Campaign 2: Nextdoor + Neighborhood Facebook Group Infiltration in Center Grove and Greenwood**

This is their home turf. We take it. Assign two dedicated field marketers to saturate Center Grove and Greenwood neighborhood Facebook groups and Nextdoor with genuine project posts — before/after photos, real customer names, hyperlocal testimonials. Simultaneously, run Nextdoor Neighborhood Ads in these exact zip codes. 

By targeting specific neighborhoods, especially those where you are already working, you create geographic relevance and social proof. Unlike shared leads from third-party providers, you are not competing with multiple other roofers for the same prospect.

 Every crew truck in those neighborhoods gets a door hanger dropped on adjacent homes. Cost per lead for this channel is a fraction of LSA. **We do not need to outspend Raptor in their backyard. We need to out-show them.**

**Campaign 3: AI Search and GBP Domination Play**

Raptor's website content is thin on educational depth. Ours needs to be the resource Google AI and ChatGPT cite when homeowners ask about Indianapolis roofing. Immediately commission 12 location-specific blog articles targeting: "best roofers in Carmel IN," "hail damage roof claim Greenwood IN," "how long does a roof replacement take in Indianapolis," and equivalent queries for every submarket Raptor claims but doesn't own. 

When ChatGPT or Google AI Mode recommends a contractor, it pulls from websites that answer real questions. "How much does a furnace replacement cost in Charlotte?" beats "We provide quality HVAC service" every single time.

 Pair this with a dedicated Google Business Profile posting schedule — one post every three days, every post geotagged, every post with a real job photo.

---

**SECTION 3: THE SINGLE MOST THREATENING MOVE THIS QUARTER**

**Launch a hyper-targeted LSA and Google Ads campaign bidding directly on Raptor's branded adjacent keywords — "Raptor Roofing reviews," "Raptor Roofing Indianapolis," "Raptor Roofing vs" — and route that traffic to a landing page titled: "Comparing Indianapolis Roofers? Here's What 2,195 Reviews Look Like."**

The page shows no competitor names. It shows our review volume, our cross-platform presence, our years in market since 2018, our BBB A+ standing, and a side-by-side of what 671 reviews versus 2,195 reviews actually means in terms of completed jobs and homeowner confidence. 

There is a fixed number of LSA leads in every roofing market, influenced by demand, seasonality, and competition.

 Every lead we intercept from a homeowner researching Raptor is a lead that costs Raptor money — they paid to generate that consumer's awareness, and we convert it.

**Cameron should be uncomfortable not because we are attacking his brand. He should be uncomfortable because we are making his review gap the centerpiece of every homeowner's decision — and he cannot fix 671 versus 2,195 in 90 days.**

This is where we win.

---

*Prepared for internal strategic use only. Recommend immediate budget alignment meeting within 5 business days.*

**Action 1: Launch an "Insurance Renewal Inspection" direct mail drop to 5,000 homes with roofs aged 10-14 years across Center Grove, Bargersville, and Whiteland this week, framed around the Fannie Mae ACV rule change.**

Above The Cut Restoration just permanently relocated to Greenwood on May 7th and is explicitly hunting the same five communities Raptor owns — Bargersville, Whiteland, Center Grove, Southport, Franklin Township. We do not wait for them to build a review base. We get to those homeowners first with a reason to call that has nothing to do with storms. The Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac ACV expansion plus carriers converting 10-15 year old roofs to depreciated coverage at renewal is the most underused lead angle in the market right now — every other roofer in Indy is still waiting for hail. Pull a list from a property data vendor (PropertyRadar, ATTOM, or LeadSherpa) filtered to homes built 2010-2016, owner-occupied, in those specific zips. The mailer is not a coupon. It is a one-page plain-English explainer: "Your insurance company may be quietly reclassifying your roof. Here's how to find out before your renewal." Free 30-minute documented inspection with a written report the homeowner can hand their agent.

The lever here is distribution arbitrage — we are reaching people before they are in-market and before they have a competitor's yard sign reference. The "I'm protecting your insurance" frame also positions Raptor as the trustworthy advisor, not a salesperson, which compounds the 5.0-star trust moat. Above The Cut is going to lead with insurance-claim advocacy as their wedge; we get ahead of them by owning the pre-claim conversation entirely.

Success metric this week: list pulled, creative approved, mail house in motion with drop date locked within 10 business days. Track by unique inbound phone number and a vanity URL. Target conversion: 0.8% inspection booking rate on the 5,000-piece drop (40 inspections), 25 of those converting through RAPTOR WINS at our 22-30% close rate.

---

**Action 2: Configure a pre-loaded storm-surge Google Ads campaign with geo-fenced rules that auto-activate within 60 minutes of an NWS severe weather warning in Johnson County.**

NWS Chicago region has logged 128 severe weather warnings through April 19th — nearly 3x the historical average — and a single hailstorm spikes search volume 200% within 48 hours. ARAC published their hail readiness guide on May 1st specifically to capture this pre-storm intent. The window after the next event will be 72 hours, and the roofer whose ad is live in the first 60 minutes captures the homeowner with an active leak who is not comparison shopping. Most accounts in this market are managed reactively — the agency notices the storm Monday morning, increases budget Tuesday, and by Wednesday the leads are already booked with whoever answered first.

Build it now, in shadow mode. Create a dedicated "Storm Response - Johnson County" campaign with separate ad groups for hail, wind, and tree-damage queries. Pre-write four ad variants that lead with "Local owner-led inspections within 24 hours" and "664 five-star reviews — Greenwood's most-trusted." Pre-load $400/day budget caps. Use Google Ads scripts or a tool like Optmyzr to monitor an NWS RSS feed and auto-toggle the campaign live when a severe warning fires for the relevant zip codes. The same script throttles LSA bid multipliers up by 40% on storm days. Pair the paid surge with a canvassing protocol: two doorknockers in trucks staged at the office, ready to roll within 90 minutes of a confirmed touchdown to the impacted streets, leaving a branded door hanger that says "We were already in your neighborhood — call us first."

The lever is response-speed as a paid-media weapon, not a sales-team virtue. Success metric this week: campaign built, dark, QA'd, with one live test fire to confirm the trigger works. CPL benchmark for the next storm event: under $85 inside 48 hours (versus $120-180 we historically see on reactive ramps).

---

**Action 3: Launch a "Real Roofs, Real Homeowners" video review-acquisition push targeting 25 completed jobs from the last 60 days, with a $50 gift-card thank-you for any homeowner who records a 60-second on-camera testimonial.**

We are at 673 reviews and adding +17 per month. Amos is adding +104, Indy Roof is adding +73, Big Sky is at +36 on a smaller base growing 11% velocity. We are getting outpaced on volume even though our 5.0 versus their 4.7-4.9 is the real moat. The text-review race is a treadmill — we need to leapfrog onto a surface competitors cannot match: video. Google's AI Overviews now mention 3-5 companies per local query and weight visual proof, review responses, and clear service signals heavily. A library of 25 authentic homeowner video testimonials, embedded on neighborhood-specific landing pages and uploaded as Google Business Profile posts weekly, becomes AEO content no competitor in Indy has at scale. Big Boy's, Trojan, and Indy Roof have zero video review presence; this is open territory.

Pull a list of the 25 highest-NPS jobs closed in March and April. The post-install accountability call (which is already a Raptor differentiator per "we don't outsource accountability") becomes the ask: "We'd love a 60-second video — what was the worst part of getting your roof done, and what made us different?" Send a videographer (or use a service like Trustmary or VideoAsk for self-recorded) to each home. The "worst part" framing is critical — authentic, slightly negative-then-positive testimonials convert dramatically better than scripted glowing ones, and they read as real to both humans and AI.
